chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), from a group of people who bought a gazelle and ate all of it while they were in the state of Ihram; what is upon them? He said:

"Upon every one who ate from among them is the ransom of game; each man among them individually bears the ransom of a complete game." And if two men hunt a game, and one of them hits it while the other does not, the ransom is upon both of them together. Narrated.

key_terms.حُرُمٌ: In the state of Ihram (pilgrimal consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ransom for eating game while in Ihram, and how does it apply to joint hunters?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) clarifies the individual liability for consuming game while in Ihram, emphasizing that each eater bears a separate ransom rather than a collective one. It further extends this principle to joint hunting, establishing that if two hunters pursue a single prey and one strikes it, both are jointly liable for the full ransom, reflecting the Shia juristic view on shared responsibility in hunting errors. This ruling is derived from the broader legal framework of expiation for Ihram violations found in the Quran.
